title: There will be higher standards for games. And actual gaming experience will be important.
author: FutureLynx_
selftext:
This sub doesnt call out games for being AI.

But at some point there will be a clear distinction between what is just low effort and what is AI and human working together to do something great.

In the end the best games will be produced by people with experience in gamedev, creative ideas, and a great passion for it.

In the past it was hard to find a gamer that was also a good creative and also had the resilience to become a good programmer, and have a consistent vision for a game.

There were many programmers working on games who weren't even gamers. And thats something that will become more important. Because testing a game and knowing if what you are doing is fun, is more important now.

Some years before AI, we saw a lot of gamedevs that were creative types, not programmer types, because of how accessible it became with game engines and tutorials.

Right now we will see people that have unique ideas, people who have been playing a specific genre everyday for decades. That know the flaws of a game like the palm of their hands and what could be improved.

comments.author: cave_men
comments.body:
"But at some point there will be a clear distinction between what is just low effort and what is AI and human working together to do something great."

Let me restate that for you:

... there will be a clear distinction between people without money (low cost modells) and people with money (high cost models).

replies.author: Such--Balance
replies.body:
I disagree.

Saw plenty of posst already of guys with deep pockets vibecoding crazy looking games over the span of a few weeks which...looked dope, but clearly missed any meaningfull gameplay loop or actual balance.

Ai still seems to suck absolute monkey balls at those.

I wonder for how long..

replies.author: Sbrazen77
replies.body:
Fax, this one guy, in what is becoming a pretty popular video, tried to vibe code a slice of World of Warcraft. I think it had $2000 behind it.

The game looks like true unplayable garbage

Hot dog water

AI game development will require creative vision  
A good sense for a solid gameplay loop  
Discernment with art direction  
System depth

And for God sakes if games are so much easier to make these days, let’s make games with some length. Why is everything a Tech demo?

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body: You can produce good work on lower models (I no longer use Fable) but it's much slower and might take much longer in real time. I spend $20 a month on my game and vibe code it in my spare time. I do have a web design, art and animation background. Someone with an agentic swarm could go circles around me but I'm just wanting to see my ideas come to life.

comments.author: NoOneKnowsSatoshi
comments.body: In the end gaming is all about entertainment. If people can enjoy game, no matter how it was made, it will succeed. All this "AI this AI that" becomes irrelevant.

comments.author: fued
comments.body:
Most AI games are slop

A lot of human made games are slop

Ai games tend to progress to finished while human slop games stop effort once they realize how bad it is

comments.author: Neither_Berry_100
comments.body: I'm one of those people you describe. I've made several games. I work together with AI and don't vibe code. I innovating a lot. I'm putting in a lot of work. My current game is still early / mid way into development. It looks good. Quite promising.

comments.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
comments.body: I mean I’ve seen people put out games that were made in a weekend. & that’s not enough time spent to catch all the bugs and nuances. To me that’s AI slop. But if you actually spent time making sure the game is a fun experience for everyone then it’s worth it.

comments.author: Such--Balance
comments.body:
Balance, 'feel', and novelty will be the 3 main factors which we as humans still have to do a lot of work for.

Novelty i would say actually slightly less with how easy ai can mix and match different genres together.

comments.author: CandidateDue2480
comments.body:
Everything you described has always been part of games, none of that is changing.

Knowing what's fun, and how to deliver a product isn't a higher requirement, it's the bar that's existed since forever. Unique ideas have been flooding the market forever. New unique ideas that can be made by less people still have to hit the same bar, no difference.

Before AI there's 4000 games released per year on Steam with 99.7% of games not turning a meaningfully fruitful enough of profit.

The difference between 4000 and 40000 games is basically nothing at this point, we are already hyper saturated.
